title: Security Holds and Damage Found on Returned Equipment Rental and Demo Kit
content:
## 1. The hold

Every agreement carries a security hold sized to the package, placed against the guest's payment method when kit is set aside rather than when it is collected. A security hold is placed only while the agreement stands in the confirmed or picked up state, that standing being read from the collective's records for the one agreement before the hold is placed.

## 2. What a technician finds

Kit handed in is checked by a technician, and what is found is recorded against the serial of the item rather than against the agreement as a whole, so two damaged items on one agreement are two assessments. Fair wear on edges and bases is not charged.

Kit that never comes back is charged at the package's replacement value rather than assessed for damage, and the waiver does not cover it.

## 3. Clauses no longer in force

The clause reading "Where the guest took the damage waiver, the collective bears the assessed amount above the package's excess and the guest bears the excess; where they did not, the guest bears the whole assessed amount" is **no longer in force**, superseded by the current basis on which the share the guest bears is settled.

The clause reading "The hold is released once the assessment is settled, in whole where nothing is owed and in part where something is" is likewise **no longer in force**, superseded by the current basis on which the amount kept back is arrived at.

Both retirements reach those sentences only. The figures each package of the Equipment Rental and Demo line carries — its security hold, whether the waiver is offered, the waiver price per day, the waiver excess, the replacement value and the release period in business days — all stand.

## 4. Releasing the hold

A hold is released only while the agreement stands in the overdue, returned, cancelled or uncollected state.

The hold is released no later than the package's release period counted in business days from the day the kit was handed in. The day the kit was handed in, as the collective's records carry it, is the anchor. Business days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, only days the collective's finance office is open counting, which excludes Saturdays, Sundays and the collective's published holidays, and business days are never mixed with calendar days. The last day of the period is itself inside it.

### The count on hypothetical dates

Take kit handed in on a Monday on a package whose release period is 3 business days, and suppose the finance office is open on each of that week's weekdays. Monday is day zero, Tuesday day one, Wednesday day two and Thursday day three. A release booked on the Thursday is inside the period, because the last day counts; a release booked on the Friday is outside it. Where the Wednesday were a published holiday of the collective, it would not count, and day three would fall on the Friday instead.

| Agreement stands | Hold may be placed | Hold may be released |
| --- | --- | --- |
| reserved | no | no |
| confirmed | yes | no |
| picked up | yes | no |
| overdue | no | yes |
| returned | no | yes |
| cancelled | no | yes |
| uncollected | no | yes |
| closed | no | no |

superseded_clauses: Where the guest took the damage waiver, the collective bears the assessed amount above the package's excess and the guest bears the excess; where they did not, the guest bears the whole assessed amount.
The hold is released once the assessment is settled, in whole where nothing is owed and in part where something is.
